fields.meta_title: High-Converting Landing Page Builder With Tests | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a high-converting landing page from a prompt: a short form, a headline test, lead alerts, and a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a High-Converting Landing Page, Then Test What Works
fields.hero_description: Build a high-converting landing page that tests its headline and saves every lead to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Six Parts That Turn Visits Into Leads
fields.features_subheading: A visitor sees one headline and a short form. Behind them, these six parts test the page and carry each lead to a person.
fields.feature_1:
A page with one goal, from one prompt

Describe the offer, who it is for, and the one action a visitor should take. Emergent builds the page with its form and the table behind it, then changes any section by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Every lead in a database you own

Each form submission becomes a row in a database you own, with the time, every answer, and the page version the visitor saw. Sort by version to see which page earned the lead.
fields.feature_3:
Headline tests you set up by prompt

Ask for two headlines and the app shows each to half of your visitors. A live dashboard counts signups per version, and one prompt puts a new line against the winner.
fields.feature_4:
Leads synced to the CRM you already use

Connect HubSpot or any other tool with an API, and each new lead reaches it with its answers and the link it came from. Sales works in the CRM while the page keeps a copy.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts for the leads worth a call today

Pick the answer that marks a lead as urgent, such as a budget or team size. The app posts each one to Slack or emails the person who follows up; other leads get a confirmation.
fields.feature_6:
Hosted on your domain, exportable as code

Publish on your own domain, which is included and uses credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository, ready for a developer to carry into your site.

fields.tab_content_1:
Cutting the form to 3 fields more than doubled requests

Kestrel Ridge Roofing used to ask 7 questions before it would quote a roof. The new page asks for 3: zip code, roof type, and phone. Per 1,000 visitors, estimate requests rose from 31 to 74. Delphine Okafor asked for a quote on a slate roof from her phone, and her request landed in the leads table.
fields.tab_content_2:
One headline won 66 demo requests, the other 38

Tallowmere sells payroll software to restaurants, and its page shows each visitor one of two headlines. After 2,400 visitors, 1,200 per headline, "Run payroll in 10 minutes after close" had 66 demo requests and "Payroll that fits your kitchen" had 38. The live dashboard still shows both counts.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each ad's keyword becomes the page headline

Pellworth Plumbing pays for a separate ad for each service it offers in Tacoma. The page reads the keyword in the ad's link and swaps in a headline to match it. A click on the water heater ad opens on "Water heater repair in Tacoma, same day." This week that ad sent 212 visitors, and 19 of them booked a visit.
fields.tab_content_4:
Remodel budgets at $40,000 or more go to a designer

Every quote request on Fernhollow Kitchens' page asks for a budget. A budget of $40,000 or more sends designer Ines Valcourt a Slack message with the answers, and everyone else gets an email with a booking link. On Tuesday, Rafe Lindqvist asked about a $52,000 kitchen, and Ines read his request in Slack.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a High-Converting Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a high-converting landing page that asks for one action and tests its headline, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one action the page asks for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the headline in plain words
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Cut the form to the fields you will use
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose a single action, such as booking a call or requesting a quote. Every section and button on the page should serve that one action. Take other links, such as your blog or careers page, off the page so a visitor has one thing to do.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the result a customer gets and how soon they get it. Read your sales call notes and reviews for the phrases people already use, and keep the headline under 10 words so a visitor takes it in at a glance.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List every field on the form and remove each one nobody would use on the first call. A roofer needs a zip code and a phone number before a site visit, not the age of the roof.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the action and the fields into one prompt, along with the headline you wrote. Emergent returns a working page with its form and a leads table behind it. Prompt again to change any section, such as moving a customer quote next to the button.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Put proof next to the button
fields.howto_step_5_des: Place one piece of proof beside the form: a short customer quote with a full name, a review count, or a row of client logos. Ask the customer before you quote them, and keep their exact words instead of a polished version.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect Slack or email for the leads that need a call the same day, and your CRM for everyone else. Submit 3 test leads, one of them a lead you would call first, and check that each one lands where it should.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish on your own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits) and leave the page alone until traffic builds. Then test one element against a second version, starting with the headline, and keep a note of each test and its result for the next page you build.

faq_plan.q: What are the best practices for creating high-converting landing pages?
faq_plan.ref: What are the best practices for creating high-converting landing pages?

prov.original: What are the best practices for creating high-converting landing pages?

faq_plan.a: Give the page one goal and one button, and build everything else around them. Match the headline to the ad or email that sent the visitor, ask only for the fields you will use, and put a named customer quote beside the form. Check the page on a phone before launch, then test one change at a time against the version that is live.

faq_plan.q: How to build a high converting landing page?
faq_plan.ref: How to build a high converting landing page?

prov.original: How to build a high converting landing page?

faq_plan.a: Decide the one action you want and the fields the form needs, then describe both in a prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It returns a working page with a leads table behind it. Submit a test lead yourself, check that the row arrived, and publish once the page reads clearly on a phone.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in high converting landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Look for what changed and what the change did to the numbers. The high converting landing page examples worth copying say what was tested: a shorter form, a new headline, a quote moved next to the button. A screenshot with no before and after shows a style, and it cannot tell you whether that style will work for your visitors.

faq_plan.q: What do high converting landing page templates get right?
faq_plan.a: They get the order right: a headline, a one-line promise, the form or button, proof, and then the details. Borrow that order from high converting landing page templates and rewrite every line for your own offer. A webinar landing page, for instance, needs the date with its time zone and what attendees will learn above the signup button.

faq_plan.q: How long should a high-converting landing page be?
faq_plan.hint: How to create a high-converting landing page in united states?
faq_plan.a: It should be as long as a visitor needs to decide, and no longer. A free quote or a newsletter signup fits on one screen, with the form right under the headline and a line of proof beside it. A higher-priced offer needs room for pricing and objections. Add those sections below the first form and repeat the button after them.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a high-converting landing page for a rental property?
faq_plan.hint: How to create high converting landing pages for rental properties?
faq_plan.a: Put the photos and the monthly rent at the top, with the move-in date beside them, since those decide whether a renter keeps reading. Below them, add a tour request form that asks for a phone number and a preferred date. Emergent can build one page for several units, with each request saved to a database you own alongside the unit it names.

faq_plan.q: What does a high-converting landing page need for business buyers?
faq_plan.a: It needs proof that a buyer can forward to colleagues, such as named customers and the problem each one solved, plus a next step like a demo. On a b2b landing page, ask for a work email and company size so larger accounts reach sales first. If IT signs off on purchases like yours, list the integrations and security answers they will ask for.

faq_plan.q: How many form fields should a high-converting landing page have?
faq_plan.a: Ask for as few fields as you will act on, and treat three as the ceiling for a first contact. Save everything else for the thank-you screen or a follow-up email, after the lead is already in. The app Emergent builds saves every submission to a database you own, where a later answer from the same person can join their row.

faq_plan.q: How do I split test two versions of a high-converting landing page?
faq_plan.a: Show each visitor one of two versions, change only one element between them, and count conversions for each. Pick the metric before launch, such as demo requests, and wait until each version has a few hundred visitors before calling a winner. Emergent builds both versions and the split from a plain-English prompt, and a second prompt starts the next test.

faq_plan.q: Why would a high-converting landing page convert worse on paid ad clicks?
faq_plan.a: Because the page does not repeat what the ad promised. A visitor who clicked an ad for one service and lands on a general page has to hunt for it. Give each ad group its own ppc landing page with the ad's offer in the headline. With the button text and the form the same across those pages, the top line is the only difference.

plan.angle: The top 10 for this keyword is example galleries (Unbounce, Dribbble), best-practice lists (Mailchimp, Shopify, Kixie, Branded Agency) and one Reddit thread asking which page converted best. They show finished screenshots or rules, never the before and after: which change moved the numbers and how the page measured it. This page shows four pages with their conversion counts and the single change behind each (a shorter form, a headline test, ad-matched headlines, lead routing), and the FAQ covers best practice, building one, examples, templates, length, rental listings, business buyers, form fields, split tests and paid traffic. Sibling primaries (ppc, b2b, webinar, real estate) stay out of headings and get links.
